medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Please contact the Office of Access, Opportunity, and Collaboration for more information.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Student organizations, including national organizations and those focused on specific student interests, will be available for students. Students will have the opportunity to expand these organizations. 

The College of Medicine supports students by providing support from the Director of Student Programs and additional activities organized by the Office of Access, Opportunity & Collaboration.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Roseman University’s Summerlin campus offers students an exceptional environment where academic excellence meets an outstanding quality of life. The campus provides the perfect balance of focused learning and vibrant community engagement, just 20 minutes away from the Las Vegas Strip.

Students enjoy state-of-the-art facilities while having access to Summerlin’s extensive network of parks, trails, and recreational amenities. Just minutes from the majestic Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area, the campus location offers unprecedented opportunities for outdoor adventure and natural inspiration. The nearby Downtown Summerlin presents diverse dining, shopping, and entertainment options, including the Las Vegas Ballpark – home of the Las Vegas Aviators – and City National Arena, the practice facility of the Vegas Golden Knights.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Roseman University does not offer on-campus housing for students. However, the Las Vegas area has an array of options to meet students' budget needs while attending school. There are housing options such as rentals and apartments near the Summerlin campus.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Please contact the Office of Access, Opportunity, and Collaboration for more information.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Wellness programming will include services designed to promote overall well-being and foster a sense of belonging. RUCOM aims to educate and promote behaviors that support medical students' emotional and physical well-being by providing free, timely, and confidential services. Students will have access to a Counseling and Wellness Center within the College as well as university resources.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: We are a program that provides individuals associated with the College the opportunity to help shape and establish its culture for years to come. As the College continues to grow, this culture is being refined and strengthened through the contributions of students, faculty, and staff. Students play a critical role in this process, actively shaping the culture and embodying the College’s vision as they navigate their educational journey and ultimately enter the profession. We recognize that our students are the future of medicine, and we view strong alignment with all participants as a vital component of our campus culture and the ability to serve our communities.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Having your own car is highly encouraged, as clinical rotations may require travel to various locations. While there may be opportunities to carpool with fellow students or utilize public transportation in certain areas, students should plan accordingly to ensure they can meet all rotation requirements without difficulty.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: RUCOM does not have a formal dress code policy for didactic courses. A Dress code is needed for anatomy lab, simulations ,and clerkships
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Office hours are provided by the faculty at the College of Medicine. Tutoring services and learning strategies workshops will also be offered by the Office of Academic and Career Advising.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Roseman University COM is committed to early experiential learning, which includes patient interactions for students throughout their GENESIS experience and the clerkship phases of the program.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Our clinical rotations include pediatrics, surgery, internal medicine, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynecology, and family medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lecture attendance is at the discretion of each faculty member teaching the course and may be required for both in-person and online sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The Roseman Readiness Curriculum is a highly integrated curriculum that emphasizes patient care in the setting of today’s advances. Diagnostic and therapeutic skills are taught from the beginning of the curriculum in the context of foundational basic and health systems sciences, with a focus on ethical principles, professionalism, and societal context. Students train to communicate flexibly, authentically, and respectfully with patients, caregivers, colleagues, and other healthcare team members to navigate a changing world effectively.

The Roseman Readiness Curriculum is competency-based and delivered in active learning formats that require students to take charge of their own learning and become lifelong learners. Groups of households in GENESIS, Roseman’s household-centered care delivery model, are managed as practices by students working with faculty physicians and interprofessional teams, merging student learning with service to the community and allowing value-based metrics to influence decision-making.

The RUCOM curriculum consists of three phases: the foundational phase, the clerkship phase, and the advanced phase.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
The College of Medicine is extremely committed to primary care and developing the next generation of physicians with values of humility, excellence, and respect.

What sets our program apart is GENESIS, our unique household-centered care delivery system, where students work alongside faculty physicians and interprofessional teams to manage groups of households. This pioneering approach merges learning with community service, allowing students to experience firsthand how value-based metrics influence healthcare decisions. Students begin with GENESIS as part of their early hands-on experience. Our 4-year program emphasizes flexible, authentic, and respectful communication with patients, caregivers, and healthcare team members
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students are required to participate with GENESIS households during their time at Roseman University COM. Additional volunteer community service opportunities will also be presented to students.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Although research is not a requirement at the College of Medicine, students who are interested in research will have the opportunity to pursue it.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Across Southern Nevada, a majority of hospitals, hospital systems, and inpatient mental health facilities have agreed to host students for our clerkships.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The practice of medicine is changing rapidly. Physicians increasingly need to understand social determinants of health, interface with emerging technology, manage knowledge streams, work in interprofessional teams and health systems, and communicate complex, personalized information to patients and families. 

Our students will be ready. 

The Roseman Readiness Curriculum is being developed as a highly integrated curriculum that emphasizes patient care in the setting of today’s advances. Diagnostic and therapeutic skills will be taught from the beginning of the curriculum in the context of foundational basic and health systems sciences, with a focus on ethical principles and societal context. Students will be trained to communicate flexibly, authentically, and respectfully with patients, caregivers, colleagues, and other members of the healthcare team to be optimally prepared to navigate a changing world.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The Roseman University College of Medicine (RUCOM) is here to produce the healthcare workforce of the future, developing clinically excellent, community-based, socially accountable, humble, compassionate, and inclusive physicians, and decrease the health disparities in Nevada. This will be accomplished by innovative teaching, emphasizing not only clinical excellence but also ethics, humility, empathy, critical and creative thinking, and real-world experience. Graduates of RUCOM will understand the complexities of communities and how the Social Determinants of Health impact both individual and population health. The communities we serve will be partners in our teaching and learning.

Mission 
To align students, educators, and the community in designing and delivering an inclusive and collaborative environment for innovative learning, healthcare, and research. 

Vision 
Diverse professionals improving the health of the region’s rural and urban communities. 

Values 
Humility 
Excellence 
Respect

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Applicants will receive an admissions offer via email. They will have a designated period to respond, in accordance with the AMCAS Traffic Rules applicable at the time of the offer.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: RUCOM has no preference for who the letter writer should be; the writer should be someone who can speak highly of an applicant’s character, academic skills, and/or their ability to pioneer a new initiative.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Applicants will be notified via their admissions portal and email if invited to an interview. As part of the interview process, they will be required to attend a virtual pre-interview session before their virtual interviews, where they will learn more about the interview process, Roseman University, the College of Medicine, student services, and more.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Applicants will participate in two 30-minute virtual interviews with faculty or senior staff leadership from the College of Medicine.
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: Applicants will have no more than two weeks to complete the secondary for best consideration, though an extension may be granted on a case‑by‑case basis. The final deadline is March 15, 2027.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: No prior relationship is required to apply.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Roseman University College of Medicine is committed to addressing the shortage of physicians in Nevada. All competitive applicants, whether in-state or out-of-state, are encouraged to apply.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: For more information, please visit our website at https://www.roseman.edu/academic-programs/college-of-medicine/
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The College of Medicine is committed to a holistic review throughout the admissions process. College of Medicine is seeking applicants who are academically competitive with a well-rounded character. The MCAT score plays a role in reviewing the competitive nature of an applicant's academic profile.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: Applicants must have completed a minimum of 90 undergraduate semester credit hours from an accredited U.S. Postsecondary institution at the time of submission.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: The Roseman University College of Medicine recognizes that applicants may follow different pathways in completing their bachelor’s degree or the prerequisite coursework needed to be a competitive applicant. The College will review all coursework to ensure passing grades and verify that the appropriate foundational material was covered. Coursework from all educational pathways will be considered.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
We are aware that students may have new experiences or updates to their originally submitted primary application. We will accept additional information such as letters of intent, updates, and notices of significant achievements to help the admissions committee fully understand the applicant. Applicants may submit up to one (1) letter of interest, update, or notice of significant achievement per academic term following the submission of their primary application or any change in their application status. Submission of these updates is not required; it is up to the applicant to determine whether an update is needed.

Applicants can email their updates in a PDF Format to CoMAdmissions@rosman.edu. Students should include their AMCAS ID in the email.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: For more information please visit our website. https://www.roseman.edu/student-experience/financial-aid/

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants must confirm their offer on the waitlist and are required to  respond by the deadline specified in their waitlist letter. Waitlist applicants will be notified of any changes.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Roseman University College of Medicine is committed to a holistic review process in seeking applicants who align with the College’s mission, vision, and values. By doing so, we create a dynamic and unique class of learners dedicated to improving the world through empathetic care, service, and advocacy. Successful applicants will be able to demonstrate their strong academic ability and commitment to improving health inequities in our communities throughout the admissions process.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The Roseman University College of Medicine recognizes that applicants have different opportunities to gain clinical exposure and shadowing experience, and does not require or recommend any specific type of shadowing. All forms of meaningful clinical exposure, regardless of setting, provider type, or format, will be reviewed and valued. The College will consider any shadowing or related experience that enhances an applicant’s understanding of the healthcare profession, including its roles, responsibilities, and the impact of social determinants of health within our communities. Experiences that meaningfully contribute to an applicant’s insight into the realities of healthcare will be considered during the admissions review process.
